samir (Customer): Hey team — since yesterday our service started getting 502/504s when calling Redwood via our VPC endpoint. Same requests from public internet succeed. Using the PrivateLink endpoint in us-east-1.
alex (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact curl and the error you see? Also do you have Private DNS turned on for the endpoint? :thinking:
samir (Customer): curl output: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
* Connected to vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: certificate subject name 'api.redwood.example.com' doesn't match 'vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'api.redwood.example.com' doesn't match 'vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com'
```
We have Private DNS disabled because we use split-horizon DNS.
maria (NetEng): That TLS error is the key. If your client resolves to the vpce private DNS name, SNI will be the vpce hostname unless you force SNI to the public host. Two options: enable private DNS so hostname resolves to Redwoods' internal DNS (and cert matches), or set SNI to api.redwood.example.com in your client.
alex (Support): Can you show `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` from an instance in the same subnet? And `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-id vpc-aaaa --filters Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.vpce.*redwood*` so we can check endpoint type/acceptance.
samir (Customer): dig shows: 10.0.5.23 (vpce ip). We explicitly wanted split-horizon so we left Private DNS off. How do we set SNI on our app? It's a Go app using net/http.
maria (NetEng): In Go you can set TLSClientConfig{ServerName: "api.redwood.example.com"} on the transport to force SNI. But long-term if you want to keep split-horizon you need to ensure cert presented by the endpoint matches the SNI. Our hosted PrivateLink usually terminates TLS using the public hostname cert when Private DNS is enabled. With Private DNS disabled the endpoint hostname will be the VPCE DNS name and cert mismatch occurs.
jen (Support): Also double-check endpoint policy and security groups attached to the interface endpoint. We saw in another customer case that an overly restrictive SG blocked the healthcheck path and produced 504s intermittently. Can you paste `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-aaaa` and the SG IDs?
samir (Customer): SGs allow 443 from our subnets, inbound only. No outbound restrictions. Endpoint policy is open right now (we tried to lock it down but rolled back). We also saw intermittent TLS alerts in our app logs before the 502s started.
alex (Support): Two simultaneous issues likely: (1) SNI/cert mismatch causing TLS failures, (2) intermittent routing to a stale ENI during AZ failover — check route table for ENI target on the prefix list. Run `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-aaaa` and paste the routes. Also check NACL logs.
maria (NetEng): If you can't change the app quickly, quick mitigation is to set up an outbound NAT (temporary) so traffic egresses via public internet to api.redwood.example.com — confirm that works. But that's not ideal for private connectivity.
samir (Customer): Quick test: routed to our NAT and curl succeeds (200). So confirms TLS name is public-only cert.
infra-bot: Auto-note: customer reported PrivateLink TLS mismatch; ticket created #INC-2026-178999. Attached logs requested.
jen (Support): Next steps for us: (A) Confirm whether your app can set SNI (preferred), (B) If not, we can coordinate enabling Private DNS on the VPCE for your VPC and provide exact DNS records to avoid split-horizon conflicts, (C) Check interface endpoint SGs/NACLs and ensure endpoint acceptance status is `available` and all AZ ENIs `in-service`.
alex (Support): Samir — can you grant read-only access or paste the outputs for the describe-* commands? We'll review and confirm. If you prefer, we can schedule a short debug call and run tcpdump on one of your instances to capture the TLS handshake.
samir (Customer): I'll paste the describe outputs in 30m. Thanks everyone. Adding the workaround to our runbook for now :thumbsup:
jen (Support): Great. I'll create a step-by-step guide on how to enable Private DNS for Redwood PrivateLink and the rollback steps for you to keep split-horizon if needed. Will post here when ready. :white_check_mark:
maria (NetEng): Also flagging to platform: we should document the SNI behavior more prominently — many customers assume the public cert will work without private DNS. filing an internal doc task.
alex (Support): Keeping ticket open. Marking as triaged. :eyes:
